expectations.text: States the Commission Q&A position (December 17, 2025): DORA applies to third-country branches in the EU if the home-country entity would qualify as an Art. 2 financial entity
expectations.evidence: 'the European Commission's Q&A of 17 December 2025 confirmed that third-country branches operating in the EU fall within DORA's scope', anchored to Art. 2 scoping.

expectations.text: Cites the Luxembourg operationalisation: CSSF's August 27, 2026 package — new Circular CSSF 26/915
expectations.evidence: 'The CSSF operationalised... on 27 August 2026 via Circular CSSF 26/915'.

expectations.text: Describes the effect: third-country branches removed from the legacy ICT/outsourcing circulars (20/750, 22/806) and brought into the DORA circular suite (including 25/882 on ICT third-party use and 25/893 on incident reporting)
expectations.evidence: 'Circular 26/915 formally moved TCBs out of those legacy [ICT/outsourcing] circulars and into the DORA-aligned circular suite': 'Circular CSSF 25/882 - governing ICT third-party use' and '25/893 - governing incident reporting' (legacy circulars described, numbers 20/750/22/806 not named).

expectations.text: Advises the practical consequence: the branch runs DORA-grade ICT risk management, third-party registers and incident reporting like an EU-incorporated entity
expectations.evidence: Branch must run its own ICT risk framework, incident reporting to CSSF (4h/72h/1-month), Register of Information, and testing programme 'as an EU-incorporated entity'.

expectations.text: Notes supervisory expectations are NCA-specific — verify the equivalent position with the relevant regulator in other member states
expectations.evidence: No statement that treatment is NCA-specific or advice to verify the equivalent position with regulators in other member states; only 'confirm... with qualified Luxembourg counsel'.
